title: Permissible Lies for Good Intentions
summary: Certain lies for peace and good intentions are permitted.
translation: Umm Kulthum bint Uqba bin Abi Mu'it (RA) narrated: I heard the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) say: ‘The person who lies to reconcile people or to convey good or say good things is not considered a liar.’ In a narration in Sahih Muslim, there is an addition: I never heard him permit any falsehood except in three cases: in war, to reconcile among people, and a man's conversation with his wife and a woman's conversation with her husband. Imam Tabari (may Allah have mercy on him) explained that in such cases, actual lying is not permissible, but rather it is about using ambiguous statements. For example, when Abu Bakr (RA) was migrating from Makkah to Madinah, someone asked him about the identity of the Prophet (peace be upon him) who was with him. Abu Bakr said, ‘He is guiding me on the way.’ The person thought it meant guiding on the physical journey, while Abu Bakr meant guiding to the path of Jannah. Hence, such statements are allowed for goodness, provided there is no intention of causing discord.
